project_metadata.name: Streamlit Calculator App
project_metadata.description: A simple web-based calculator application built with Streamlit that supports four basic arithmetic operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division

dependencies.name: streamlit
dependencies.purpose: Web UI framework for building interactive, reactive single-page data applications

file_inventory.summary: Main and sole application entry point that renders the calculator UI and executes arithmetic operations using Streamlit's reactive execution model.
file_inventory.description: This file constitutes the entire application, merging UI rendering with business logic in a single top-to-bottom script. It presents a two-column numeric input form alongside an operation selector, groups them inside a Streamlit Form to prevent premature re-runs, then routes the submitted values to the appropriate arithmetic handler. A division-by-zero guard is enforced before any division is attempted, halting execution gracefully. Results are rendered in a success banner and made available in a collapsible details panel.
business_rules: Division by zero is not permitted; an error message is displayed and script execution is halted immediately via st.stop()
Both numeric inputs default to 0.0 and accept up to 6 decimal places of floating-point precision
Exactly four arithmetic operations are supported: Add, Subtract, Multiply, and Divide
Addition is pre-selected as the default operation (index=0)
The result is displayed as a formatted equation: num1 SYMBOL num2 = result
Computation details (first_number, second_number, operation, result) are exposed in a collapsible expander panel
All inputs are grouped inside a single form; calculation is triggered only on explicit form submission

error_handling.prevents: Undefined result variable access, ZeroDivisionError exception

module_structure.description: The entire application resides in one Python script (app.py) with no modules, packages, helper files, class definitions, or standalone functions. Logic flows linearly from top to bottom following Streamlit's reactive re-run execution model, where the entire script re-executes on each user interaction.

architecture_patterns: Reactive script execution — Streamlit re-runs the full script on every user interaction
Form-based input batching — st.form groups inputs so calculation triggers only on submit
Early-exit error handling — st.stop() halts execution after validation failure
Top-to-bottom linear control flow with conditional branching on submitted state
